verse.text: “A new command I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another.

reflection.scripture: “A new command I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another.
reflection.observation: Jesus spoke these words to His disciples during the Last Supper, right before His betrayal and crucifixion. This wasn't a suggestion — it was a new command, replacing the old covenant with something radically different. The standard isn't just 'be nice' or 'treat others fairly.' It's 'as I have loved you' — a self-sacrificing, unconditional, servant-hearted love. And He gave this command knowing full well how flawed His disciples were. He didn't wait for them to get it right first.
reflection.application: Today, who in my life is hardest to love? Maybe it's a coworker, a family member, or even myself. The call isn't to manufacture warm feelings — it's to choose the same kind of love Jesus showed: patient, forgiving, present. One practical step: before reacting to someone difficult today, pause and ask, 'How has Jesus loved me in my worst moments?' Then extend that same grace.
reflection.prayer: Lord, Your love for me is relentless — even when I'm stubborn, distracted, or distant. Thank You for not giving up on me. Today, help me love others not because they deserve it, but because You've shown me what love really looks like. Give me patience when I'm irritated, kindness when I'd rather withdraw, and courage when love feels costly. Let my life reflect Your love to someone who needs it today. Amen.
